messages:
Aria: Quick brain dump from today's sync — proposing a small pilot to split the monolithic 'inference-orchestrator' into two bounded services: routing (stateless) and session-store (stateful). Hoping to get feedback on ownership, migration steps, and rollback safety.
Jon: love the split idea. main risk is session migration + tenant skews. what's the pilot scope? :eyes:
Aria: pilot scope: 1) route-only traffic for read-mostly tenants, 2) mirror-write sessions for a subset, 3) measure latency/cost. Not doing full cutover in pilot.
Priya: 👍 on mirror-write. do we have tooling for divergence checks? we used something similar for config-store extract.
Theo: we can reuse the diff-runner from config-store with small tweaks. infra-bot: tool status — diff-runner v2 deployed to staging, docs at https://infra.redwood/internal/diff-runner.
Jon: ownership question: who owns the new session-store? operations? platform? product infra?
Aria: thinking: session-store ops-owned for runtime and backups; routing remains inference team-owned. But a "contract guardian" (rotation role) will own the API contract and test suite.
Priya: rotation role is good. prefer 3-way on-call overlap during first 2 weeks of pilot.
Theo: agree. also suggest a "migration fence" adapter pattern: keep a shim that implements the existing API but forwards to new service based on header flag. That lets us flip per-tenant without global cutover.
Aria: yes — adapter + header gating. I'll add a canary plan: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% by tenant cohorts if error rate < 0.5% and p95 latency delta < 20ms.
Jon: can we automate the ramp based on SLAs rather than manual? ops team can own runbooks but automation would reduce cycle time.
infra-bot: FYI — router supports weighted rules via policy v3. Example: 
```
policy:
  - match: tenant in ["team-a"]
    weight: 10
    target: session-store-v2
  - else: session-store-v1
```
Priya: excellent. for migrations we'll need a small audit log of decisions per tenant + rollbacks. stdout logs are messy; recommend a single migration-events stream to Kafka.
Theo: +1. also we should cap the memory footprint of sidecar adapters — last pilot caused a 60MB tail at peak. infra-bot: recent metric — adapter-sidecar mem 55-70MB on p3-small (95th). Link: https://perf.redwood/internal/adapter-sidecar.
Aria: noted. keep adapter light. If memory is an issue we can bundle smaller shim inlined in binary as fallback.
Jon: technical debt prioritization: how do we decide which debt items to address before pilot? I worry unknown debt will block cutover.
Priya: propose a preflight checklist (short):
- list of all callers + dependency graph (call sites)
- top 5 risky flows (based on error logs)
- migration test harness + diff-runner config
- rollback plan + owner contacts
- perf baseline for routing + session-store
Aria: will add that to the RFC. Also recommending a debt-bucket: any item with severity >=3 (out of 5) must be fixed or mitigated before ramp beyond 10%.
Theo: governance question: should we allow teams to opt into co-ownership? e.g., small infra teams might not be able to own a service end-to-end.
Aria: propose: owners must be able to deploy, oncall, and fix P1s. if a team can't, they need to designate a co-owner or rotate with platform.
Jon: metrics to track during pilot: p50/p95 latency, error-rate delta, cost tokens/sec, divergence rate from diff-runner. Also time-to-rollback if we flip a tenant.
Priya: add compatibility metric: % of responses passing contract assertions. target 99.9% for pilot.
Aria: I'll draft the follow-up RFC with: goal, scope, preflight checklist, canary knobs, ownership matrix, and migration playbook. Looking for reviewers by Wednesday.
infra-bot: created epic: SERVICE-DECOMP-397654 (https://boards.redwood/internal/epics/397654).
Theo: last note: keep service API minimal. prefer 3 primitives: CreateSession, FetchSession, SnapshotSession. Everything else via adapters.
Jon: agreed. small APIs lower coupling.
Priya: I'll volunteer to run the diff-runner configs and own the contract tests for wave 0.
Aria: thanks! pulling this into RFC draft now. Ping if you want to pair on the checklist.
Jon: thanks team. short-term action items: Aria -> RFC draft by Wed, Priya -> diff-runner config, Theo -> adapter resource budget proposal, infra-bot -> attach perf links to epic.
Aria: will do. closing thread.
